entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Jos 22:1-9 . Joshua Dismisses the Two Tribes and a Half, with a Blessing.

entries.heading: 3. Ye have not left your brethren these many days unto this day
entries.text: 3. Ye have not left your brethren these many days unto this day --for the space of seven years.

entries.heading: 4-7. get you unto your tents
entries.text: 4-7. get you unto your tents --that is, home; for their families had been left in fortified towns ( Nu 32:17 ).

entries.heading: 8. he spake unto them, saying, Return with much riches
entries.text: 8. he spake unto them, saying, Return with much riches --in cattle, clothes, and precious metals. divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren --(See on Nu 31:25-39 ).

entries.heading: Verse 10
entries.text: Jos 22:10 . They Build the Altar of Testimony on Their Journey.

entries.heading: 21. Then the children of Reuben . . . answered
entries.text: 21. Then the children of Reuben . . . answered --repudiating, in the strongest terms, the alleged crime, and deponing that so far from entertaining the intention imputed to them, their only object was to perpetuate the memory of their alliance with Israel [ Jos 22:24, 25 ], and their adherence to the worship of Israel's God [ Jos 22:26, 27 ].

entries.heading: 33, 34. the thing pleased the children of Israel
entries.text: 33, 34. the thing pleased the children of Israel --The explanation not only gave perfect satisfaction to the deputies, but elicited from them expressions of unbounded joy and thankfulness. "This day we perceive that the Lord is among us" [ Jos 22:31 ], that is, by His gracious presence and preventing goodness, which has kept you from falling into the suspected sin and rescued the nation from the calamity of a fratricidal war or providential judgments. This episode reflects honor upon all parties and shows that piety and zeal for the honor and worship of God animated the people that entered Canaan to an extent far beyond what was exemplified in many other periods of the history of Israel.
